subject.title: fix(qqbot): bound remote media downloads with header and idle timeouts

question: Should QQBot enforce a fixed 30-second body-idle timeout for existing remote-media downloads, accepting failure for any transfer that makes no progress for that long?
rationale: The implementation prevents indefinite resource retention, but the exact no-progress budget changes observable behavior for existing slow or intermittently stalled upstream media sources.

options.title: Accept the 30-second boundary
options.body: Merge after refresh if the QQBot owner agrees that failing a transfer after 30 seconds without any body data is the intended availability tradeoff.

options.title: Choose a different policy
options.body: Request a different QQBot-owned idle budget or an explicitly documented alternative if known upstream transfer characteristics make 30 seconds too aggressive.

recommendation.title: Accept the 30-second boundary
recommendation.body: Merge after refresh if the QQBot owner agrees that failing a transfer after 30 seconds without any body data is the intended availability tradeoff.
